name: Hashishene

papers.title: Multidimensional analysis of cannabis volatile constituents: identification of 5,5-dimethyl-1-vinylbicyclo[2.1.1]hexane as a volatile marker of hashish, the resin of Cannabis sativa L

evidence: Measured in 3 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.24–0.37% of total volatiles (0.048–0.074mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Hashishene is a volatile aroma molecule that contributes to the distinct scent of aged cannabis resin. Chemically, it is a terpene formed when plant resins are exposed to light and oxygen. You are most likely to encounter it in the concentrated resin of the cannabis plant.
consumer_summary.found_in: It is famously found in hashish, the concentrated resin of Cannabis sativa L., where it serves as a unique chemical marker.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to hashishene because it acts as a specific chemical fingerprint for hashish, helping analytical chemists trace and identify cannabis products. They are exploring how it forms through photochemical processes and oxidation-reduction when plant resins age. The current literature consists entirely of analytical bench science (Oxford level 5), focusing on its identification and structural properties rather than biological effects.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: The only available evidence is analytical bench science (Oxford level 5) focused on identifying the molecule in plant resins.
